name: NY-22
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about four points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent John Mannion has a large financial advantage, outraising Buller roughly ten to one
Prediction markets price Democratic win chances around 94-95 percent

model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Mannion: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge, with markets pricing the race as near-safe for Democrats. With no polls to contradict that picture, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based expectation of a double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Buller competitive would be the first real signal that this race is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-22 is a central New York House district that leans Democratic by about four points, and first-term incumbent John Mannion is seeking reelection. He enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised about $2.7 million and holding $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Kailee Buller has raised roughly $267,000 with under $200,000 available. No outside groups are active against Mannion.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Mannion's win probability around 94 to 95 percent. The combined evidence points to a comfortable Democratic margin in the mid-to-high teens, consistent with the district's lean, incumbency advantage, and resource gap.
